Publisher XML converted to located text (jats_text): abstract and figure/table captions only
pages_convention: XML section and paragraph locators (jats_text) for the abstract (§0 ¶1) and captions (labels as printed, e.g. Fig. 6); printed journal pages for body text, which the XML extract omits (printed pages coincide with PDF pages counted from 1)

entry.evidence: The results in literature indicate the need to develop a fast forecasting method that can be applied for a large number of clusters

sequences.source_document: Gentili & Di Giovambattista 2022, PEPI 327:106879 (PDF body text; XML abstract and captions)

steps.action: Pose the question of forecasting, within hours to days of a strong earthquake, the probability that a strong subsequent earthquake (type A cluster) will follow.
steps.quote: analyses seismic clusters to forecast strong earthquakes of magnitudes similar or greater to those of the mainshock

steps.action: Take over the NESTORE machine-learning classifier (per-feature one-level decision trees combined by a Bayesian rule) from the authors' 2017 and 2020 papers.
steps.quote: of the previous machine learning method, named NESTORE (Next STrOng Related Earthquake)

steps.action: Revise NESTORE_M2 for California: nine features on events with M ≥ Mm-2, time-dependent completeness from the Helmstetter et al. (2006) equation, start time 1 min, and intervals from 6 h to 7 days.
steps.quote: In this paper, we applied a revised version of the NESTORE_M2 method to California seismicity

steps.action: Revise the inherit-and-validation block. The earlier version kept inherited thresholds and blamed their performance drop on small samples; the new version re-checks hit rate against false-alarm rate by leave-one-out (LOO) because of a cluster selection effect.
steps.quote: Further tests demonstrated that this is not always correct because there is a selection effect on the clusters.

steps.action: Select SCSN catalog data from 1981 onward and an onshore study polygon, using local completeness (maximum curvature plus 0.2 for clusters of at least 80 events, otherwise Mc = 3), CompletenessWeb and published completeness maps.
steps.quote: For our analysis, we selected data from 1981 to the present

steps.action: Design the cluster identification: a window-based method with the Gardner-Knopoff time window and the Kagan (2002) space window, chosen by comparing the window areas with Zaliapin & Ben-Zion nearest-neighbour cluster areas.
steps.quote: For this reason, we adopted the Kagan (2002) equation for space-window evaluation.

steps.action: Extract clusters with o-mainshock M ≥ 4, excluding Dm in [0.8–1.2]: 79 clusters, of which 50 (21 A, 29 B) remain after 6 h; the class balance shifts with time (Fig. 5a).
steps.quote: The algorithm for cluster identification extracted 79 (50 A and 29 B) clusters inside the selected area.

steps.action: Compare cluster class with o-mainshock magnitude, depth and rake: no relation found; the rake data are too few to be statistically relevant.
steps.quote: For California, we did not find any relationship between the o-mainshock magnitude or depth and the cluster class

steps.action: Train feature thresholds, validity intervals and probability vectors on each leave-one-out training set of the 50 clusters.
steps.quote: testing each cluster after training obtained by all other clusters

steps.action: Compare LOO performance with random guessing in ROC and precision-recall graphs: reliable at all intervals, best at 12 h, with recall and precision falling for T > 3 days.
steps.quote: For all time periods, NESTORE’s performance is always in the upper left triangle for ROC graphs

steps.action: Test eight well-known M ≥ 5.8 clusters individually (Fig. 7). All A clusters, including the retrospective Ridgecrest 2019 forecast, are correct; Hector Mine becomes correct after 1 day; North Palm Springs fails as an outlier.
steps.quote: Ridgecrest 2019, a cluster correctly classified as A, can be considered a retrospective forecast

steps.action: Examine how feature thresholds and their reliability vary across the LOO training sets (Table 2, Fig. 9) to locate unstable features and intervals.
steps.quote: We investigated differences in the thresholds found by different training sets in the training phase of the LOO method.

steps.action: Build rNESTORE: keep only intervals where at least 95% of training sets find a threshold, use jackknife-mean thresholds, and recompute probability vectors; this drops SLcum and QLcum2 and the Q feature for Ti < 5 days.
steps.quote: We developed a more stable classifier for future classification, called rNESTORE

steps.action: Self-test rNESTORE on the full training dataset (Fig. 8): performance is stable and improved for Q and Z, flagged as a test of internal coherence only.
steps.quote: in this case, the training set and test set are coincident

steps.action: Test NESTORE and rNESTORE on an independent set of 11 clusters (3 A, 8 B) from ComCat for northern California and from SCEC 2020 onward, with completeness estimated for this test set.
steps.quote: To test rNESTORE on an independent database, we used for northern California the Comprehensive Earthquake Catalog

steps.action: Compare the two classifiers on the independent set (Fig. 11): both are perfect at 0.5–1 day; rNESTORE correctly classifies Ocotillo Wells at 2–3 days where NESTORE fails; one A cluster is misclassified at 6 h.
steps.quote: Both methods correctly classify all clusters for time intervals 0.5–1 day

steps.action: Compare which features succeed in California with the authors' earlier results for Italy and NE Italy-W Slovenia: N2, Vm and Z work at short times in all three; Q and QLcum are region-dependent.
steps.quote: The N2, Vm, and Z features showed good short-term performance after o-mainshock for all three studies.

steps.action: Keep the claim that NESTORE and rNESTORE forecast type A clusters reliably, best at 0.5–1 day, and name productivity, magnitude irregularity and event concentration as SSLE precursors, pending a larger database.
steps.quote: Both algorithms provide the best performances for intervals of 0.5–1 day.

tree.answer: Yes; 50 training clusters plus 11 independent clusters
LOO tests, case studies, threshold variation across training sets, and an independent test set; mostly survives, with outliers and weakness at longer times
Kept: classifier performs better than random, best at 12 h

end.claim: NESTORE, trained on 50 southern California clusters, forecasts type A clusters better than random at all intervals (best at 12 h: FPR 0.17, TPR 0.80, precision 0.76 in LOO tests), and its jackknife version rNESTORE classifies all 11 independent clusters correctly at 0.5–1 day.

decisive_move.sentence: The leave-one-out comparison of NESTORE's ROC and precision-recall performance against random guessing on the 50 clusters is what establishes the classifier's characterized skill.

gates.evidence: Action: the data are an existing catalog, selected for completeness, not acquired to test a hypothesis. Claim: LOO tests and the 11-cluster independent test could have placed the classifier at or below random guessing (p. 9, 11–12). Registration: feature definitions, time intervals (inherited from 2017) and reliability rules were fixed before the independent test, but ThMc = 80 was chosen by trial and error and rNESTORE was built after the LOO results were seen (p. 6, 10).

imports.item: precision-recall graphs for imbalanced classes (Saito & Rehmsmeier 2015)

novelty_claims.quote: we propose an innovative machine learning approach [...]
In addition, we propose a new, more robust approach, called rNESTORE, that can reduce overfitting problems

limits: The XML extract contains only the abstract and captions, so body steps are located by printed pages. No peer-review file was supplied (the paper only thanks anonymous reviewers), so no review sequence is coded. The rNESTORE self-test (Fig. 8) is not counted as a V check because training and test sets coincide. The independent test set is small (11 clusters, 3 A, none A after 3 days), so its results depend on few cases. Sub-claims and their statuses: (1) rNESTORE outperforms NESTORE at 2–3 days, estimate_with_resolution at best, resting on one cluster (Ocotillo Wells) (inference); (2) high productivity, magnitude irregularity and event concentration are SSLE precursors, best_explanation without stated rivals and supported by cross-region consistency with the authors' own earlier studies; (3) the Ridgecrest 2019 retrospective forecast is a single case. No rival hypotheses are tested, and the composition is coded capability_first as the closest fit for a method-characterization walk (inference). Feature and interval choices were partly made by trial and error and after seeing LOO results; the effect of alternative choices (ThMc, Dm exclusion band, minimum magnitude) is not reported. The sequence order follows the text; the actual order of work is not documented (inference).

disagreements.target: Vorobieva and Panza (1993); Vorobieva (1999) voting-based SSLE prediction
disagreements.support: Argues from the literature that a 10–40-day window misses many SSLEs (71% in Italy) and that voting gives only a binary output; no new test is run against the method.
disagreements.quote: The main drawback of the Vorobieva and Panza (1993) and Vorobieva (1999) methods is that forecasting requires a long time span T

disagreements.target: Gulia and Wiemer (2019) b-value-based foreshock/aftershock discrimination
disagreements.support: Cites the ongoing debate (Brodsky; Dascher-Cousineau et al.; van der Elst) and argues that reliable b-values need more events than catalogs usually provide; no own test.
disagreements.quote: the main problem in the applicability of the method for real clusters of seismicity is the need, for correct estimation of the b-value

disagreements.target: Gentili and Di Giovambattista (2020): inherited thresholds and the reading of later performance drops
disagreements.support: Further tests showed a selection effect among late-SSLE A clusters, so the drop is not only a small-sample effect; the validation block is revised accordingly.
disagreements.quote: Further tests demonstrated that this is not always correct because there is a selection effect on the clusters.

disagreements.target: Gentili and Di Giovambattista (2017, 2020): reliability of the Q feature at short intervals
disagreements.support: rNESTORE's threshold-stability analysis shows Q is unstable in California at short times, so it is used only at longer intervals.
disagreements.quote: in previous works was considered reliable even for small time intervals
